question: Which of the following groups of major river systems formed the Northern Plains of India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra are three major river systems originate in the Himalayas and flow through the north and east of India, depositing vast amounts of fertile alluvial soil over millions of years, forming the vast and fertile Northern Plains.
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in Asia streching for about 3200 kms, flowing through Pakistan, India, and China.
 
 
• It is also known as the Sindhu River in India.
 
• It originates from the Bokhar Chu glacier in the Tibetan Plateau.The glacier is located near Lake Mansarovar in the Great Himalayas.
 
 
 
• The** Brahmaputra River **traverses **Bangladesh**, **Northeastern India**, and **Tibet (China)**.
 
 
• It is **referred **to as the **Siang/Dihang River in Arunachali**, the Brahmaputra or **Luit in Assamese**, the **Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibetan**, and the **Jamuna River in Bengali**.
 
• It **rises **in Tibet, China's **Chemayungdung glaciers** and **travels 3,848 kilometers** (2,391 miles) before draining **into the Bay of Bengal**.
 
• By discharge, it ranks as the 9th largest and 15th longest river in the world.
 
 
 
• The **Ganges River**, sometimes referred to as the Ganga, is a transboundary river that travels through **Bangladesh**, **India**, and **Tibet's Himalayan ranges**.
 
 
• As the goddess Ganga, it is revered as the** most sacred river in Hinduism**.
 
• The Ganges is the** longest river in India** and, in terms of discharge, the 3rd largest river in the world.
 
• At an elevation of roughly 13,800 feet (4,200 meters), the **Gangotri Glacier **in the Himalayas is the **source** of the Ganges River.
 
• The river **travels approximately 2,500 kilometers** or 1,560 miles before **spilling into Bay of Bengal**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Godavari:

 
 
• It is a river that flows through the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in India.
 
• It is also known as Dakshin Ganga.
 
• It flows into Bay of Bengal.
 
 

 
• Narmada:

 
 
• It is a river that flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat in India.
 
• It flows into Arabian sea.​
 
 
 
• **Tapi:**
 
 
• is a central Indian river.
 
• It originates in the Eastern Satpura Range of southern **Madhya Pradesh **state.
 
• It flows in a westward direction, draining some important historic places like Madhya Pradesh’s Nimar region, East Vidarbha region, and Maharashtra’s Khandesh in the northwest corner of the Deccan Plateau and South Gujarat before draining into the Gulf of Cambay of the Arabian Sea.
 
• The River Basin of Tapi River lies mostly in the eastern and northern districts of Maharashtra state.​
 
 
 
• Kaveri (**Cauvery)**:
 
 
• ​It rises on the Brahmagiri Hill of the Western Ghats in southwestern Karnataka state.
 
• It flows through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and **descends the Eastern Ghats** in a series of great falls.
